[[Image:Sinner Zverev Princess of Wales Wimbledon 2026 (cropped).jpg|thumb|Runner-up Alexander Zverev and the winner Jannik Sinner receiving the trophy after the final]]

Defending champion [[Jannik Sinner]]<ref>{{cite web|last=Jurejko|first=Jonathan|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/tennis/articles/c5ykw5n0p7no|title=Sinner beats Alcaraz to win first Wimbledon title|date=13 July 2025|website=BBC Sport|access-date=4 June 2026}}</ref> defeated [[Alexander Zverev]] in the final, 6–7<sup>(7–9)</sup>, 7–6<sup>(7–2)</sup>, 6–3, 6–4 to win the gentlemen's singles tennis title at the [[2026 Wimbledon Championships]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/tennis/jannik-sinner-wimbledon-defence-prince-paris-b3013515.html|title=Jannik Sinner defends Wimbledon title with battling win against Alexander Zverev|publisher=The Independent|date=12 July 2026|accessdate=12 July 2026}}</ref> It was his second [[Wimbledon Championships|Wimbledon]] title and fifth [[Grand Slam (tennis)#Tournaments|major]] title overall.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/tennis/articles/c78y2eqq317o|title=Sinner holds off Zverev to defend Wimbledon title|publisher=BBC Sport|date=12 July 2026|accessdate=12 July 2026}}</ref> Zverev was the oldest man in the [[Open Era]] to reach the finals of all four majors for the first time, at {{ayd|1997|4|20|2026|7|10}} old.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://en.tennistemple.com/actu/zverev-becomes-oldest-man-to-reach-all-four-grand/aVJw |title=Zverev becomes oldest man to reach all four Grand Slam finals|date=10 July 2026 |accessdate=25 August 2026}}</ref><ref> {{cite web|url=https://www.ubitennis.net/2026/07/whos-on-course-for-us-open-glory-after-wimbledon-twist-and-turns/|title= Who’s On Course For US Open Glory After Wimbledon Twist And Turns?|date=24 July 2026| accessdate=26 August 2026}} </ref><ref name=WimbyFinal26>{{cite web|url=https://www.atptour.com/en/news/zverev-fery-wimbledon-2026-friday|title=Zverev ends Fery's dream run, reaches first Wimbledon final|date=10 July 2026|accessdate=10 July 2026|website=atptour.com|publisher=Association of Tennis Professionals}}</ref>

With his first-round victory, [[Novak Djokovic]] continued a 21-year-long streak of having never lost in the opening round of Wimbledon, and became the first player in the Open Era to win more than 80 opening-round matches at the majors.<ref> {{cite web|url=https://www.thetennisgazette.com/news/novak-djokovic-makes-tennis-history-at-wimbledon-after-winning-first-round-match/|title= Novak Djokovic makes tennis history at Wimbledon after winning first-round match|website=TheTennisGazette|date=29 June 2026}} </ref> During the tournament, he surpassed [[Roger Federer]]'s record of Wimbledon men's singles match wins, reaching 107.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.atptour.com/en/news/djokovic-safiullin-wimbledon-2026-sunday|title=Djokovic ends Safiullin's run & breaks Federer's Wimbledon record|date=5 July 2026|accessdate=5 July 2026|website=atptour.com|publisher=Association of Tennis Professionals}}</ref> The quarterfinal match between Djokovic and [[Félix Auger-Aliassime]] was the longest quarterfinal in tournament history, at 5 hours and 15 minutes long.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.wimbledon.com/en_GB/news/wimbledon_2026_auger-aliassime_djokovic_qf |title=Djokovic survives longest-ever Wimbledon quarter-final |date=7 July 2026|accessdate=7 July 2026|publisher=Wimbledon|website=wimbledon.com}}</ref> At {{ayd|1987|5|22|2026|7|9}} old, Djokovic was the second-oldest Wimbledon semifinalist in the Open Era, only behind [[Ken Rosewall]] in [[1974 Wimbledon Championships – Men's singles|1974]] (aged {{ayd|1934|11|2|1974|7|3}}).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://tennishead.net/he-is-the-only-man-older-than-novak-djokovic-to-reach-the-wimbledon-semi-finals/|title=He is the only man older than Novak Djokovic to reach the Wimbledon semi-finals|publisher=Tennishead|date=9 July 2026|accessdate=10 July 2026}}</ref>

[[Arthur Fery]] was the second [[Wild card (tennis)|wildcard]] to reach the Wimbledon semifinals in the Open Era, after [[Goran Ivanišević]] in [[2001 Wimbledon Championships – Men's singles|2001]],<ref name=WimbyFinal26 /><ref>{{cite news |title=Wimbledon 2026 results: Arthur Fery stuns Flavio Cobolli to reach semi-finals |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/tennis/articles/c5yzvnxg6ygo |access-date=8 July 2026 |work=BBC Sport |date=8 July 2026}}</ref> the first unseeded British player at Wimbledon and the first British male wildcard at any major to do so in the Open Era.<ref> {{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/tennis/story/_/id/49307168/british-wild-card-arthur-fery-shocks-flavio-cobolli-reach-wimbledon-semifinals|title= Wild-card Arthur Fery upsets Flavio Cobolli to reach Wimbledon semis|date=8 July 2026|website=[[ESPN]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Botcherby |first1=Live Reporting Elizabeth |last2=Beardmore |first2=Michael |last3=McKenna |first3=Chris |last4=Sian |first4=Millie |last5=Pearson |first5=Nicola |title=Wimbledon 2026 LIVE: Arthur Fery beats Flavio Cobolli |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/tennis/live/czjwnmle9p3t?post=asset%3Ad194dde3-f722-4193-b9d0-416063a8bb84#post |date=8 July 2026|access-date=8 July 2026 |work=[[BBC Sport]]}}</ref>
Aged {{ayd|1990|4|25|2026|7|5}}, [[Jan-Lennard Struff]] became the oldest first-time major quarterfinalist in the Open Era.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.atptour.com/en/news/hurkacz-struff-wimbledon-2026-sunday|title=Struff makes history as Hurkacz retires in fifth set of Wimbledon R4|date=5 July 2026|accessdate=5 July 2026|publisher=Association of Tennis Professionals|website=atptour.com}}</ref>
